pedagogy.title: Why NEUTRAL in an 80%+ earnings beat environment?
pedagogy.content: An 80%+ earnings beat rate sounds bullish — and it is for individual stocks. But the regime classification looks at cross-asset signals, not just equities. VIX at 18.3 is moderate: it's not the sub-16 reading that signals institutional complacency (RISK-ON) nor the 22+ that triggers caution (EARLY RISK-OFF). Brent crude at $126 is the key friction — high energy prices act as a tax on consumption and compress discretionary spending, adding an inflation headwind that keeps credit markets cautious. The Dow's -1.13% Friday vs Nasdaq's -0.19% tells the story: big-cap tech is holding up, but cyclical/industrial bellwethers are rotating out. In a NEUTRAL regime, our edge comes from picking the stocks where the earnings beat has already de-risked the binary event, leaving a clean technical structure. That's why MSFT, AAPL, META, and NVDA dominate this scan: the news is in, the positioning is known, and the chart pattern provides the entry/exit discipline.

macro_thesis:
Regime call: NEUTRAL. The S&P 500 is hovering near fresh highs with 80%+ earnings beats, but the VIX at 18.3 and Brent at $126 prevent a clean RISK-ON signal. The market is digesting an extraordinary earnings season while navigating an elevated energy price environment and mixed geopolitical signals. This is a stock-picker's environment: the index is going sideways, but individual names with earnings de-risked offer clean technical setups.

Conviction story #1 — Post-earnings mega-cap tech. MSFT (Azure +37%, AI capex validated), AAPL (iPhone + Services strong), META (ad revenue beat, Reality Labs improving), and NVDA (structural AI demand, no earnings risk until May 28). These are the four horsemen of Q1 2026: all reported, all beat, all have clean charts above key moving averages. MSFT above SMA50 $396 is the most technically clean. AAPL near 52w high $288 is the breakout candidate. META below SMA50 $630 is the pullback-to-strength entry. NVDA is the structural momentum play with the lowest near-term event risk.

Conviction story #2 — Visa as quality compounder. V at $326.99 above SMA50 $310 with cross-border volume acceleration is the non-tech quality anchor of this scan. Payment network, not lender — sharia-compliant, R/R 1:1.6 (best in scan). Diversification anchor away from tech concentration risk.

Conviction story #3 — Global diversification via energy, gold, APAC. TTE at near 52w high riding Brent $126 is the EU energy play. GLD above SMA200 $391 provides NEUTRAL-regime safe-haven ballast. EWJ at $88 captures Nikkei momentum and yen-weakness export tailwinds. RACE (Ferrari) is the EU luxury pullback — SMA50 $347 pullback entry with luxury pricing power as fundamental anchor.

Risk to thesis: AMD miss tonight rippling into NVDA. Brent above $130 = inflation panic. CPI hot May 13. Stops are hard — trail to breakeven after TP1.
